properties.name: A hub, or any set of designs the person may read, is opened ON DEMAND as one view — N open stores read through one key space namespaced by graph_id — over which every ordinary reflow2 tool runs unchanged; a write through the view lands in the design that owns the node; releasing the view changes nothing, because nothing was copied
properties.statement: reflow2 SHALL serve a VIEW over N designs held in one process: an agent names a set of graph_ids (a hub's members, or any set the host says the caller may read) and receives one session whose key space is the union of those designs, each id namespaced by its graph_id, so every ordinary tool (search_design, get_node, detect_gaps, propagate_change, seam_coverage, what_next, loop_status, the review relations) runs over the view with no new tool and every id in every reply names its owning design. The view is NOT a copy: it reads the open stores directly, so it cannot go stale and there is nothing to merge back; releasing it costs nothing. A WRITE made through the view lands in the design that owns the node it changes, under that design's single-writer lock; an edge between nodes of two designs is recorded in the design that makes it, as dec:idea-a-relation-between-nodes-in-two-designs-is-recorded-so-linking-works-on-the-one-design settled, never in a third place. PERMISSION IS PER WRITE AS WELL AS PER READ: the host passes the readable set and the writable set; a write into a design the caller may only read is refused naming that design; a design outside the readable set is absent from the view and the view says it is absent without saying what it held. Memoised per-design derived scans (gaps, defects) are COMPOSED from per-design results, as compose_and_analyse already does, not recomputed over the union. CONSEQUENCE FOR HUBS: a hub holds membership and the view, never a copy of a member, which retires the stale-copy problem (a suspended watch, external_dependency pins owed) at its root; the hub-side use is integrated-flo's and flo2's, the primitive is reflow2's. Builds on req:every-cross-design-operation-takes-its-other-designs-by-graph-id-under-the-hosts-read-filter (the named operations by graph_id come first and the view reuses their resolver) and on compose_and_analyse's namespacing (req:composed-analysis).
